$comment: THE ISA, ONCE: the opcodes of the bytecode every board's VM and the IDE's simulator run. tools/gen_isa.py writes src/isa_ops.gen.h from it; the IDE keeps a byte-identical copy (lib/isa.json, checked in its CI) and generates its Opcode type. The wire format is textual (one instruction per line), so the order here is not a wire number. Add an opcode here first, then run the generators.

opcodes.name: ADD
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a + b

opcodes.name: SUB
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a - b

opcodes.name: MUL
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a * b

opcodes.name: DIV
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a / b (0 when b is 0)

opcodes.name: GT
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a > b

opcodes.name: LT
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a < b

opcodes.name: EQ
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a == b

opcodes.name: AND
opcodes.doc: pop b, pop a, push a && b

opcodes.name: TONE
opcodes.doc: square-wave tone on a passive buzzer; 0 = off

opcodes.name: DIST
opcodes.doc: push the ultrasonic distance in cm

opcodes.name: INFER
opcodes.doc: push the latest class index (0 = none)

opcodes.name: PIXN
opcodes.doc: set up the LED strip: count pixels, all off

opcodes.name: PIX
opcodes.doc: pop colour (0xRRGGBB), pop index (-1 = all): colour a pixel

opcodes.name: DTEXT
opcodes.doc: a row of the screen is this text

opcodes.name: DNUM
opcodes.doc: pop a number, append it to the row
